name: capture-page-text-to-field
summary: Park whole-page OCR text into schema fields on initialize, so an LLM/reasoning field (which cannot read the document) has content to work with.

first_page_field.description: schema id receiving the FIRST page's text; plain string field, ui_configuration.type 'data'

last_page_field.description: schema id receiving the LAST page's text; on a 1-page document it receives the same text as first_page_field

max_chars.description: per-field truncation cap; keeps a long page from bloating the annotation and the downstream prompt

provenance: Lifted from a field-built function hook (2026-07). Verified live on a 6-page and a 1-page document, and the page_data semantics re-verified against a purpose-built 25-page document: the 20-page default, the silent >20 truncation, ascending result order, and texts-has-no-position all confirmed by API probe.
notes: Reasoning fields are feature-gated and separately billed — confirm the org has them before designing around this. Fails OPEN: any fetch/parse error logs and writes empty strings rather than blocking the document. Uses granularity=texts so no line joining or reading-order reconstruction is needed. Requires sideload: ["schemas"] on the hook (TxScript) — clearing it fails every run before any useful work. Pairs with a reasoning field naming these fields in its context; prefer two narrow labelled fields over one concatenated blob, since context entries are presented to the model by field label.
